provenance: sc-2272 triage; PR #533 closed as not a bug (the caps are physical-line hard caps)

external.text: eslint/max-lines options: max (default 300) — maximum number of lines allowed per file; skipBlankLines (default false) — whether to ignore blank lines when counting; skipComments (default false) — whether to ignore comments when counting.

prompt:
## Problem Statement
The comment firewall (guard-comments) makes agents keep a justified comment, but the size caps — the 500-line file cap and the per-function caps — count comment lines too. Justifying a comment can therefore push a file over its cap, and agents end up deleting small functions to buy line budget back. Comment lines the firewall requires should not count against the size caps.

## Symptoms & History
One ship went 494 → 497 → 499 → 501 → 503 lines across attempts as justified comments were added; the agent removed two small helper functions to get back under 500.

## Dependency & Context
devkit's size ratchet (guard-size, `maxLines` in guard.config.json), the generated eslint `max-lines` / `max-lines-per-function` rules, and the comment firewall under gate-engine/comment-firewall.

## What's Been Tried
Proposed: set `skipComments: true` on max-lines and max-lines-per-function, or give lines under an approved rationale a bounded allowance.

gold.desc: Identifies that the repository's own recorded policy caps RAW physical lines, comments included (the size cap asks whether a unit is too big, the firewall whether a comment is justified), so the premise that required comments should not count contradicts a settled decision.

decoys.desc: Recommends excluding comment lines from the size count (skipComments: true, or reusing the comment firewall's meaningful-line test) as the way forward.

provenance: int-frink-wake-hold (mined); t3code pinned at the last main commit before the row was added
prompt:
## Problem Statement
Our Electron app runs an AI CLI through its SDK and reads the response stream per-turn: a request handler awaits the turn, persists the assistant message when the turn's result frame arrives, and stops reading. When the agent backgrounds work (subagents, monitors, long commands), the CLI speaks again later — so we need a reliable way to decide when the model is REALLY finished. The current stand-down heuristic reads the Stop hook's background_tasks snapshot, and it keeps losing the final answer. How should we improve the stand-down decision?

## Symptoms & History
Five fixes on this axis in six days, each repairing the last one's damage: a 5-burst wake cap killed a live 20-minute build; removing the cap left chats advertising 'working' forever; letting the agent's own done-signal outrank the task list killed a live subagent; narrowing that still dropped the final answer; a bounded 500ms drain window narrowed the race but a late burst is still lost silently.

## Dependency & Context
@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, consumed via query() returning one long-lived stream per session. Electron main process persists messages to SQLite.

## What's Been Tried
Burst caps, wall clocks (rejected), agent-declared done overrides, subagent vetoes, a stream-confirmed drain window.

gold.desc: Identifies the session-lifetime stream consumer pattern (t3code's takeWhile-on-explicit-session-stop over the same SDK) as making the per-turn 'is the model done' decision unnecessary — the wait the heuristic serves need not exist.

decoys.desc: Recommends improving the stand-down heuristic itself (a smarter background_tasks check, a longer or adaptive drain window) as the way forward.

provenance: int-ship-resume-partial-fix (mined from sc-4095 triage); devkit pinned at the parent of the residual fix #818

external.text: fix(ship): record the invocation when guard-size or hook-source preflight blocks, so --resume replays it. The blocking preflights (size, hook source, dist integrity) now run after record_ship_intent exists, and still before any branch or worktree is created. They fail through a single helper, ship_abort_resumable. It records the attempt unless one is already recorded, then exits with the preflight's own status. Deliberately unchanged: identity and collision refusals still do not record.

prompt:
## Problem Statement
`devkit ship --resume <branch> -- <extra paths>` lets an agent add extra files to a resumed ship. When the resumed run aborts at a preflight, the extra paths are silently dropped: the next resume does not know about them and the agent believes they were staged. Reproduced when the size preflight (guard-size) refused the resume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A resume that aborts at a preflight keeps its extra paths for the next resume,
- or at least stops discarding them silently (the abort names the extra paths it did not record).

## Symptoms & History
Seen twice in one week, both via the guard-size refusal. One earlier fix touched this script.

## Dependency & Context
ship is a bash script (ship-branch.sh) driven by a TypeScript CLI; the extras are recorded to the resume state file only after all preflights pass.

## What's Been Tried
Nothing yet.

gold.desc: Names the exits that still drop the extras silently (the directory-path refusal, the --body-file exits, or another exit before record_ship_intent) as the remaining work, while crediting PR #701 for the guard-size trigger.

decoys.desc: Endorses closing the problem as already fixed by PR #701 / adopting it as the whole answer.
